title: stochastic-page-lock-coalescence-debug-and-mitigation-plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We are observing long-lived GPU memory residency and stochastic fragmentation correlated with continuous batching + KV cache prefetch patterns. Unlike classical slab thrashing, this appears driven by page-locked allocations and partially-freed arenas that prevent coalescence across stream-synced free windows. The immediate symptoms are sustained growth of active device memory and occasional OOM on long-running inference pods under steady throughput.

Goal:
- Root-cause the allocator behavior that leads to page-level fragmentation and delayed slab coalescence under cudaMallocAsync and our multipool strategy.
- Propose and validate mitigations that reduce steady-state resident footprint by >= 30% without regressing latency SLOs.

Repro steps observed so far:
1) Run continuous batching harness (mixed prompt lengths, 1.2x baseline throughput) with KV cache prefetch enabled and hot-slice retention.
2) After ~6–12 hours, host traces show repeated allocation spikes during small batches and a drift in cudaMallocAsync arena residency.
3) nvprof/CUPTI sampling shows many small device frees that are queued on non-default streams; cudamallocasync pages remain mapped longer than expected.
4) Grafana memory heatmaps show high fragmentation index in high-util hosts.

Hypotheses:
- When frees occur on auxiliary streams, cudaMallocAsync defers merging of freed pages until an internal epoch or stream-synchronization point, leaving lots of small free fragments (page-locked) that cannot be coalesced with adjacent free pages.
- Our multipool size classes and early-KV prefetch pattern create many same-sized small allocations across streams, which then free in interleaved ways preventing slab-level coalescence.
- Continuous batching with bursty tail latency causes frequent short-lived allocations that the async allocator holds onto for reuse, but the reuse patterns across kernels mismatch, causing resident set growth.

Data collected (attached links):
- Grafana dashboard (live): https://grafana.redwood/team/gpu-memory/d/fragmentation-harness
- Perf traces (GDrive): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c/kv-prefetch-traces-2026-02-20
- Sampling script repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator-sampling/tree/eng/kv-harness

Experiments performed and findings:
- Experiment A (force frees onto default stream): routing frees to the default stream reduced mapped residency by ~18% within 2 hours but increased p99 tail for small-batch latency by ~8ms. Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5221
- Experiment B (increase small-pool eviction aggressiveness): reduced fragmentation index by ~12% but caused an uptick in allocation churn for hot models (extra small allocations created), showing a workload-dependent tradeoff.
- Experiment C (coarse-grained KV prefetch window): delaying KV prefetch batching to align with existing batching windows reduced cross-stream interleaving but increased cold-start latencies for first requests.

Decisions & trade-offs so far:
- We will not immediately force all frees onto the default stream due to the measurable p99 latency regression for latency-sensitive customers. We will keep that as an opt-in canary for Dedicated customers.
- Prioritize implementing an allocator-side heuristics prototype that opportunistically coalesces page runs when the host is below a configurable tail-latency pressure threshold. This is expected to improve steady-state without global stream synchronization.

Next steps (owned):
- [Arjun] Build a deterministic stress harness that can reproduce the page-lock coalescence failure in < 4 hours on a c5-gpu-standard node. Target: 2026-03-05.
- [Maya] Add allocator sampling counters and a lightweight tracing hook to correlate free-stream ids with page-run fragmentation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator-tools/pull/87. Target: 2026-03-08.
- [Infra] Deploy a canary with the sampling build to 2 pods in staging and collect 72h traces. Contact: infra-oncall@redwood.com. Target: 2026-03-10.
- [Arjun + Runtime] Prototype coalescence heuristic: attempt local page run merges when (a) free-run neighbors are present, (b) future predicted reuse is low (based on LRU sampling), and (c) no latency-critical inflight requests. Target initial prototype: 2026-03-18.

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket:
- Reproducer reliably demonstrates reduced resident set after prototype change by at least 30% at steady state, or
- We ship an opt-in per-tenant setting (force-sync frees) with documented p99 trade-offs and a rollback plan, or
- We produce a runbook and mitigation plan (config knobs + scheduling changes) that reduces customer OOM incidents by 90% in staging.
